test.title: login API returns a token
test.error:
Error: expect(received).toBe(expected) // Object.is equality
Expected: 200
Received: 423

triage.reason: The login endpoint returned HTTP 423 Locked, not a wrong business value. On the public practicesoftwaretesting API, 423 is the documented response for an account locked out after repeated failed login attempts, so the shared demo account 'customer3@practicesoftwaretesting.com' is locked. The test's request and its expectation of 200 are both reasonable, and the app is responding correctly per spec, so this is neither a real bug nor a broken script. Failure on all 3 attempts matches a persistent account lock rather than a timing race, and the sibling /products test shows the host is reachable, ruling out a connectivity fault.
triage.evidence: "Expected: 200 / Received: 423" at `expect(response.status()).toBe(200);` for POST https://api.practicesoftwaretesting.com/users/login with data { email: 'customer3@practicesoftwaretesting.com', password: 'pass123' } — 423 is "Locked".
triage.next_step: Manually POST to /users/login with those credentials (e.g. curl) to confirm the 423 body/message, then unlock or reset the customer3 demo account (or switch the test to a dedicated, non-shared account) and re-run the @smoke suite.

triage.reason: The locator hint is a red herring: the fill() timed out because the login page never rendered. The accessibility tree shows the server itself answered the navigation with an Apache-level 404 ("Not Found ... The requested URL was not found on this server", Apache/2.4.52 at with-bugs.practicesoftwaretesting.com), so goto('/auth/login') never reached the app's login screen and no email textbox could exist. A page the test needs is broken/not served, consistently across all 3 attempts — that matches "a page the test needs is broken". The main alternative is a broken script (the login route having been renamed, e.g. to /login, leaving the page object out of date); the 404 coming from Apache rather than from the SPA's own router is what tilts this toward a server/app-side problem rather than a stale path.

triage.next_step: Open https://with-bugs.practicesoftwaretesting.com/auth/login in a browser (and curl it for the status code): if it 404s, file it against the app/deployment (missing SPA rewrite or broken route); if it loads, compare the real login URL and update LoginPage.goto().

triage.reason: The mock route pattern is too narrow, so it never intercepted the real products request. Playwright matches globs against the full URL including the query string, and the home page fetches products with query params (pagination/price/sort). As a result the real API data was returned and rendered, so the empty-state message correctly did not exist. The accessibility tree proves real products loaded (nine product links plus a 3-page pager), which means the mock was bypassed rather than the app misbehaving. Identical failure on all 3 attempts rules out flakiness.
triage.evidence: Test code: `await page.route('**/products', (route) => route.fulfill({ status: 200, json: { data: [] } }));` vs. the rendered page: `link "ECO Combination Pliers CO₂: A B C D E $14.15"` and `navigation "Pagination": ... listitem: page 2` — while the error says `Locator: getByText('There are no products found.') ... Error: element(s) not found`.
triage.next_step: Change the route pattern to also match query strings (e.g. `page.route('**/products?**', ...)` or a regex like `/\/products(\?|$)/`), then re-run with a trace and confirm in the Network tab that the products request was fulfilled by the mock.

Meanwhile the app clearly worked: the Pliers checkbox is checked and the grid shows only 'Combination Pliers' and 'Pliers'. Identical failure on all 3 attempts rules out flakiness; a network/environment fault is excluded because the page and filter rendered fine.
triage.evidence: Code line 16: `(response) => response.request().method() === 'QUERY' && response.url().endsWith('/products'),` versus page state `checkbox "Pliers" [checked] [active] [ref=e83]` and rendered results `heading "Combination Pliers"` / `link "ECO Pliers ... $12.01"`; error `Error: page.waitForResponse: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded.`
triage.next_step: Record the real filter call (run with `--debug` or add `page.on('request', r => console.log(r.method(), r.url()))`) and change the predicate to match it, e.g. `(response) => response.request().method() === 'GET' && response.url().includes('/products') && response.url().includes('by_category')`.

triage.reason: The click on "Add to cart" worked — the cart badge in the nav shows 1 — but no confirmation toast/alert exists anywhere in the page tree, and there is no alternative wording of a success message that the locator could have missed. This fits the app's "Bug Hunting Mode" state, which already shows other injected UI defects on the same page ("Contakt", "Reltded products", Home link pointing to #/contact). A changed-message-text (broken script) explanation is less likely because no comparable text appears at all, though it cannot be fully excluded without checking the app's notification component.
triage.next_step: Manually add "Combination Pliers" to the cart in chromium and watch the notification area (or inspect the toast/alert component in the app source) to confirm whether any success message is rendered at all, or whether its wording changed from "Product added to shopping cart."
